citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
An APHIS official observed one male Highland cattle with a noticeably thin body condition. This animal was housed in the
same primary enclosure with two other Highland cattle, including a littermate with an appropriate body condition.
According to facility representatives, this condition had not been noted prior to the inspection; therefore, this condition had
not been communicated to the attending veterinarian. A thin body condition can indicate underlying disease or nutritional
deficiencies. The facility must ensure that animals are observed daily for their health and well-being and that problems of
animal health, well-being, and behavior are conveyed to the attending veterinarian in a timely manner. To be corrected by
October 16, 2026.

An APHIS official observed one female Patagonian cavy with multiple scabs on the back near the base of the tail and one
female Patagonian cavy with a smaller number of scabs on the back, in mixed-sex housing with 18 other cavies.
According to facility representatives, this has happened previously and may be caused by altercations between animals or
breeding behavior, but they have not made adjustments to mitigate the social incompatibility. Incompatibility between
animals may result in wounds or other health impacts such as those observed in the two Patagonian cavies. The facility
must ensure that animals housed in the same primary enclosure are compatible. To be corrected by October 16, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
